cards.text: It's the fifth month of the fourth year of Zedekiah, king of Judah, and the prophet Jeremiah has a yoke on his neck, because the LORD told him to wear it as a sign to serve the king of Babylon. Then another prophet comes up to him: Hananiah son of Azzur, from Gibeon. And friend, Hananiah does NOT pull him aside for a quiet little chat.

cards.question: Where does Hananiah say his piece to Jeremiah, with the priests and all the people watching?

answers.text: In the house of the LORD

cards.question: Hananiah says the LORD of Hosts has a message, and it goes like this: I have broken the ___ of the king of Babylon.
Hananiah says the articles that Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, carried off from the house of the LORD will be brought back. How soon?
Hananiah also says the LORD will bring back Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, the king of Judah who was carried off to Babylon, along with all the exiles from Judah. True or false?

cards.text: Now Jeremiah answers Hananiah, with the priests and all the people standing right there. Two prophets face to face in front of EVERYBODY, and friend, the last standoff I saw like this was two bakers and the last cookie on the tray.

cards.question: Jeremiah's first word back to Hananiah is "Amen!" True or false?

cards.text: And I bet he means it: may the LORD bring the articles and the exiles back from Babylon. Then he says "Nevertheless," and friend, that's the prophet version of "I LOVE your cookies, BUT."
Jeremiah says the prophets of old, the ones who came before him and Hananiah, prophesied war, disaster and plague against many lands and great kingdoms.

cards.question: Jeremiah says a prophet who prophesies peace will be recognized as truly sent by the LORD only if his word comes ___.

cards.text: Hananiah's next move isn't a speech. He takes the yoke right off Jeremiah's neck.

cards.question: Hananiah has the yoke from Jeremiah's neck in his hands. What does he do with it?

answers.text: He throws it in the fire

cards.question: Then Hananiah tells all the people that in this way, within two years, the LORD will break Nebuchadnezzar's yoke off the neck of all the ___.
Right after Hananiah breaks the yoke, Jeremiah fires back at him with a new word from the LORD on the spot. True or false?

cards.text: Jeremiah just goes on his way, and friend, if somebody snapped MY handle in front of a crowd, you'd hear me yelling from the Dorinverse. But shortly after, the word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah.

cards.question: The LORD sends Jeremiah back with a message for Hananiah: Hananiah broke a yoke of wood. What does the LORD say Hananiah has made in its place?

cards.text: The LORD says He has put a yoke of iron on the neck of all these nations to make them serve Nebuchadnezzar, and they WILL serve him. He's even given him control of the beasts of the field.

cards.question: Jeremiah tells Hananiah: Listen, Hananiah! The LORD did not send you, but you have persuaded this people to trust in a ___.
Then Jeremiah gives Hananiah the LORD's word: the LORD is about to remove him from the face of the earth. When does the LORD say Hananiah will die?

cards.text: The LORD says it's because Hananiah has preached rebellion against the LORD. Hananiah promised two years, and in the seventh month of that very year, the prophet Hananiah died.

findings.problem: Card 1 cites "Jeremiah 27:2, 12; 28:1", a list of separate verses that crosses into the previous passage. The citation rule wants one span from the first verse used to the last. Here that span would be Jeremiah 27:2-28:1, which takes in far more than the card uses. The output format only describes single references and hyphen ranges.
findings.question: When a story card draws on non-contiguous verses, including verses from the previous context passage, how should its "verses" field be written? Is a comma or semicolon list like "Jeremiah 27:2, 12; 28:1" allowed? Or should the card cite only the passage verse it tells (Jeremiah 28:1) and treat the yoke background as context without a citation?

findings.problem: Card 9 is a flat restatement of Jeremiah 28:8 with no storyteller line, reaction or voice. It reads like a summary, not Papa Dorin telling the story.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. The question has just said "a yoke of wood," so "A yoke of iron" mirrors that wording. Both wrong answers are "of bronze" ("Shackles of bronze" and "Bars of bronze"), so the bronze pair makes the right answer the odd one out. The wrong answers should differ from each other and stay parallel to the right one, for example by using different materials and including another yoke option.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: "Hananiah promised two years" renames what the text calls a prophecy. Hananiah proclaimed, "This is what the LORD says" (Jeremiah 28:11), and Jeremiah calls them "the words you have prophesied" (Jeremiah 28:6). Calling it a promise makes it Hananiah's own pledge.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
